courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: With all the icons and splashscreens added, let's deploy the applications and let's start with Android.
For that,
visit your Android Studio project and there under build,
you can generate assigned bundle or APK which is what we need to do here.
Now leave the default Android app bundle checked and click next and
now you need a keystore or you can create a new one.
Choose a path for that keystore first of all and that can simply be your project path which is what I'll
choose here,
so I'll add it, my keystore here in my project path.
Assign a password, one that you should of course remember,
you can leave the alias here as it is and assign another
password here,
leave the validity,
then enter some data about yourself.
This is all data that is basically used for signing the app and signing is a process that basically makes
sure that you are the owner of the app,
you are the creator and you are the only one to change that app or to manage that app. The exact data
you fill in here of course doesn't matter but it should be truthy because that is what you kind of use
for signing and what you kind of leave as a footprint here
and with all that, you got a new keystore.
You can leave everything as it is here
and then choose a build type which should be release and finished it
and what this will now do is it will take your application and put it into an APK, so into a bundle
which you can upload to the Play Store and sign it with your data to add some proof that you are a creator
of this application and to kind of link it to you
you could say. So let's wait for this build to finish and once this is done, you can upload this. For
that, you can search for Google Play Store Console to find that management area for you as a developer.
There you need to sign in with your Google account and then you need to accept the developer agreement
and pay a one-time registration fee which isn't too high, it's no subscription, it's just one time,
this is basically there to make sure that only people that have at least some serious intentions release
apps to the App Store.
Now here I am locked in after accepting the agreement and paying that fee
and here, you can now click create application, choose your default language, give it a name like PairBnB
or whatever the name of your application of course is, click create here and then here, you need to
fill out information about that application, upload some images and basically build that page
your app will have in the App Store and of course therefore, you definitely want to add information
here that makes people want to download it.
Now what you of course need to do also is under app releases here, you can upload a new app release. For
that, go to production track and click manage, create a release,
continue here
and now browse files and upload your APK.
Now where do you find that? It's in your project folder under Android app, release, release and that is your
app bundle and now this gets upload here, is processed and thereafter once you also finish the
rest here, you can publish this app bundle and that is how you deploy your app to Android.
